transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Nguyen (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Linda Park (Arbor Head of ML), Raj Patel (Platform Eng), Tom Henderson (CFO)

Auto-generated summary: (may be imperfect)
- Goal: discuss upcoming renewal, capacity upgrade to dedicated pool, and additional region support (EU + APAC).
- Customer wants predictable latency for peak trading windows, data isolation, and enterprise controls (SOC2, KMS).
- Redwood to send updated pricing and run benchmark for eu-west-1.

Topics:
- Renewal terms and timing
- Dedicated capacity sizing and cost vs hosted tradeoffs
- Region expansion and VPC options
- Security/compliance items required for sign-off

Transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call 	5 Sophie here from Redwood, Marco is on the line too. Linda, Raj, Tom you with us?
[00:15] Linda Park: Yep, hi Sophie, hi Marco. Linda on my end.
[00:20] Raj Patel: Raj here.
[00:25] Tom Henderson: Tom, thanks.
[00:30] Sophie Nguyen: Great. The purpose of today's call is the renewal and expansion check in for Arbor Finance 	5 looking at the upcoming contract, you mentioned wanting dedicated capacity and an EU region 	5 so we want to align on sizing, timeline, and security items.
[00:48] Linda Park: Correct. We're looking at July renewal but would like to lock pricing now if possible; main ask is a 3 node dedicated pool for inference with eu-west-1 availability. Peak windows hit pretty hard for quote generation. Latency spikes are our main pain.
[01:10] Marco Alvarez: Thanks Linda. Just to clarify, when you say 3-node, is that a conservative baseline or expected sustained concurrency? What's your target p95 latency and tokens per second?
[01:25] Linda Park: Target p95 under 200ms for short prompts (<128 tokens). Throughput during peak is about 30-50 requests per second across our web tier, but some bursts to 100 for batched jobs.
[01:40] Raj Patel: And we want to keep data in EU for regulatory reasons, and we have VPC peering requirements 	5 basically private connectivity.
[01:50] Marco Alvarez: Understood. A couple notes: dedicated pools give you isolated GPU capacity and predictable throughput; we can pin model versions. For EU region we can provision dedicated nodes in eu-west-1 but there's a lead time for capacity reservations. Also we can enable VPC peering / private endpoints.
[02:15] Tom Henderson: From finance side, we care about unit economics. Can you walk through cost delta between hosted vs dedicated? We saw an initial estimate but want line item detail.
[02:30] Sophie Nguyen: Sure. I'll send an updated quote that shows per-month committed cost for a 3-node dedicated pool vs projected hosted spend based on current usage. Marco will run a short benchmark to validate latency numbers so you can see expected tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:47] Linda Park: Also SOC2 is a gating requirement for us. We need audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and SAML SSO.
[02:58] Marco Alvarez: We have SOC 2 Type II reports available, integrate with customer KMS (we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys), and SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. We'll share the security pack.
[03:15] Raj Patel: Any caveats around KV cache or stateful sessions in dedicated? We use KV caching for session reuse in some flows.
[03:28] Marco Alvarez: The runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching. On dedicated, you get control over cache sizing per node and we can tune the eviction policies. There can be warmup time; we'll capture that in the benchmark.
[03:45] Linda Park: Sounds good. Also curious about fallbacks: if dedicated capacity is saturated, what's the fallback? We don't want outages in trading hours.
[03:58] Sophie Nguyen: We can configure smart routing: primary to dedicated pool, automatic fallback to a hosted-compatible variant. You can set failover thresholds and throttling. There are tradeoffs 	5 fallback may have slightly different model variant or higher latency.
[04:20] Tom Henderson: Okay. On contract length, is there any discount for 12 vs 24 months? Also do you offer committed burst capacity?
[04:32] Sophie Nguyen: Yes, longer-term commits have bigger discounts. We can include burst capacity options for peak windows 	5 typically on a per-month add-on. I'll include both 12 and 24 month pricing scenarios in the quote.
[04:45] Marco Alvarez: For the benchmark, we'll simulate 50 rps sustained with bursts to 100 to match Linda's numbers. We'll run in eu-west-1 and capture p50/p95/p99 latency and GPU utilization.
[04:58] Raj Patel: For VPC, we prefer Transit Gateway peering rather than single-host peering. Can you support that?
[05:08] Marco Alvarez: We support multiple peering models; I'll include the network diagram options in the security pack. There are small differences in setup time.
[05:20] Linda Park: One more thing 	5 data retention settings. For regulatory we need logs for 7 years. Is that supported?
[05:28] Sophie Nguyen: We have configurable retention for logs and observability; we can export logs to your S3 or SIEM. Seven years is long but manageable as an add-on. We'll note that in the security doc.
[05:42] Tom Henderson: Back to pricing, what about overage protection during spikes? We don't want surprise bills mid-month.
[05:50] Sophie Nguyen: We can set hard caps and alerts; overages can be auto-billed or throttled depending on your preference. We'll show that in the quote options.
[06:05] Linda Park: Timeline 	5 we need EU region online before June to run our internal QA. Is that feasible?
[06:13] Marco Alvarez: Lead time depends on exact capacity and current inventory. I can check and aim to provision by mid-May if we agree soon. If we need APAC as well that's additional lead time.
[06:25] Raj Patel: APAC is desirable but not mandatory for this renewal; it's for Q4 planning. EU first.
[06:32] Sophie Nguyen: Understood. We'll prioritize EU.
[06:36] [00:06:40] Marco Alvarez: Quick note 	5 some of our customers use quantized model variants to reduce cost; that may impact p95 slightly but helps economics. Would Arbor consider a quantized variant for some workloads?
[06:55] Linda Park: Possibly, but for risk-sensitive flows we need model fidelity. We could pilot quantized for lower-risk batch jobs.
[07:06] Tom Henderson: If quantization affects quality, we want an SLA or rollback policy.
[07:12] Marco Alvarez: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback. We'll include a plan for quality monitoring and evals tied to your prompt sets.
[07:25] [00:07:30] Linda Park: OK, what are the next steps?
[07:28] Sophie Nguyen: I'll send the updated quote and the security pack (SOC2, KMS details, network diagrams) by Friday. Marco will kick off the benchmark and share results in a spreadsheet. We should plan for a follow-up sync next week to review the benchmark.
[07:44] Raj Patel: Can Marco share the exact test harness so we can reproduce it in our environment?
[07:48] Marco Alvarez: Yes 	5 I'll share the load test script and the runbook.
[07:53] Tom Henderson: Finance will need a formal PO path 	5 once we have pricing and SOW we'll engage procurement.
[07:59] Sophie Nguyen: Great.
[08:02] [00:08:10] (some cross talk)
[08:15] Linda Park: One transcription nit: I think earlier you said 'KV cache' as 'K V cache' weirdly on your doc, but we understand.
[08:23] Marco Alvarez: Yep, Fireflies sometimes splits acronyms.
[08:27] [00:08:40] Sophie Nguyen: Any blockers from Arbor side for us to proceed?
[08:32] Linda Park: Need to confirm VPC peering model and get procurement timeline roughly 3 weeks once quote received.
[08:40] Raj Patel: I'll pull the network team in for the peering decision.
[08:44] Tom Henderson: We'll try to move quickly on the PO once numbers look reasonable.
[08:49] [00:09:10] Sophie Nguyen: Cool. Recap of action items: Sophie send quote + pricing scenarios, Marco run benchmark in eu-west-1 and share runbook, Linda confirm peering choice. We'll reconvene next Tuesday.
[09:05] Linda Park: Works for me.
[09:07] Raj Patel: Fine.
[09:09] Tom Henderson: Good.
[09:11] Sophie Nguyen: Thanks everyone. Ending call.

Call end.
